A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE-based LMM interpretation and steering work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original IoU, CLIP-score, GPT-4o/human consistency results, and feature-steering and hallucination case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds layer/model evaluations, quantitative steering results, and a 100-example hallucination experiment.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.4 retain the TopK SAE, masked top-five-image interpretation, feature clamping, and attribution procedures. Applying the framework to additional layers and models does not introduce a documented algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 adds an object-steering scenario using a pure-white image and the question 'What do you see in this image?' Training/cache dataset sources and the HallusionBench task remain unchanged; additional models and a larger hallucination sample do not themselves constitute new datasets.

E2.justification: The original interpretation comparisons retain their Random baseline. v2 adds a random-selection control to the quantitative steering comparison in Table 9. InstructBLIP and Qwen are models being interpreted, rather than competing interpretation methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations at LLaVA layers 8, 25, and 32 using SAEs reported with k=4096 and 100 analyzed features. InstructBLIP uses CLIP-only evaluation because it has 32 image tokens. New protocols also include 100-object-neuron screening with GPT relevance scoring from 1 to 10 and a 100-example HallusionBench intervention study. The original main setup is retained.

E4.justification: New layer and architecture ablations examine dependence on depth and backbone (Sections 3.3–3.4 and Appendix I). Quantitative object steering and the expanded hallucination intervention analysis substantially extend v1's illustrative cases. The sadness case is retained in Appendix E, not removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 random-baseline IoU runs and 30 CLIP-score runs with 99% confidence intervals. v2 adds no new repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practices for its additional experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. Added results include layer IoUs of 0.30/0.31/0.40, InstructBLIP CLIP scores of 28.01 versus 17.71 random, Qwen CLIP scores of 27.99 versus 18.22, and steering scores of 6.36 versus 2.02. Only 11 of 100 object neurons change outputs; Table 11 reports 9 improved, 89 unchanged, and 2 worsened hallucination cases. These are new evaluations, not same-setting gains over v1. Table 10's IoU scaling is unclear.

T1.justification: The SAE equations, activation-averaging definitions, steering formulation, and logit-difference attribution derivation are retained. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the specific suggestion that interpreting LMM features could illuminate human multisensory integration and foregrounds discovered neuron types instead. The central interpretation, steering, and error-localization contributions remain, as does the abstract's general brain-parallel statement.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added layer/model results as evidence of generality and newly discusses steering's dependence on prompts and inhibition by other neurons. Appendix J characterizes hallucination reduction as preliminary potential. Existing attribution explanations and the main limitations discussion are retained.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that 60 human-evaluation samples receive two expert judgments each, yielding 120 evaluations; v1 specified 10 samples per concept without the annotator count. This does not establish a larger sample. Settings for the new ablations and steering tests are added, while existing prompts, implementation tools, and the GitHub access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to InstructBLIP, BLIP-2, and Neo et al.'s visual-information interpretation work, and removes Quiroga et al.'s invariant-neuron reference and associated introductory comparison. It also positions quantitative steering evaluation as an exploratory gap. The main related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites contribution bullets, condenses several Section 4 paragraphs and the conclusion, moves the sadness case to the appendix, and changes supplementary sections to lettered appendices. Affiliations and acknowledgments are updated. The overall narrative structure and most methodological prose remain.

P2.justification: Five compact result tables are added: Tables 3, 4, and 9–11. Existing figures and prompt tables are retained, with relocation and renumbering, including sadness moving from Figure 5 to appendix Figure 16. The graphics and two-column presentation otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The layer/model checks and 100-case hallucination experiment strengthen evidence beyond v1's single-model/layer evaluation and illustrative steering, including reporting unsuccessful interventions. The benefit is limited by selected-case steering scores, sparse details for some new experiments, and Table 10's unexplained IoU scaling. The revision improves empirical support without establishing broad steering reliability or generalization.
